questions: Reading taken: both optional moves were made (PastInextensible.of_retraction and pastExtensible_of_subArc). They are pure curve topology with no Cauchy surface. PastInextensible.of_retraction is the one-sided twin of Inextensible.of_retraction and now sits right after it. pastExtensible_of_subArc is a sub-arc lemma and now sits in § 4, the sub-arc form. PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy keeps (2.4), its tail-free case, its other forms and its witnesses. The move reverses with no other change, because no name changes.

Reading taken on 'Docstrings move with their declarations': all five moved. Three are byte-identical. In PastExtensible.of_top_tail one sentence, and in FutureExtensible.of_top_tail the second half, described Extensible.of_top_tail's former pause construction. After the refactor that construction no longer exists, so those sentences would be false, and they were rewritten (declarations[0..1].docstring). Extensible.of_top_tail's docstring now describes its new proof. The statements are untouched in every case.

Reading taken on placement: pastExtensible_of_subArc goes in § 4 inside `section … variable {C : Causality M} {W : Opens M} … end`. That keeps its text byte-identical and its binder telescope (M, the instance, C, W, then its own binders) unchanged, which the dump confirms. The alternative was the end of § 2, inside the first `namespace Causality`, which also has those variables in scope.

findings: Library, not paper: the pause construction is now written once. Extensible.of_top_tail is a 3-line corollary of PastExtensible.of_top_tail (no pause) and FutureExtensible.of_top_tail (the pause), through extensible_iff. Its 95-line proof is gone, and the module loses no statement.

Library, not paper: moving the five lemmas into SubArc changed no proof term (Expr.hash), although SubArc's closure lacks Causal.CauchyDual and it opens Filter and Topology besides. kb/0083's risk did not arise.

Library, not paper: PastInextensible.of_retraction's term-mode matcher (PastInextensible.of_retraction.match_1_1) has the same type and value hash as Inextensible.of_retraction.match_1_1. Placed in the same module, after it, it was not shared: it keeps its own name and its parent's value hash is unchanged. So within a module Lean 4.31 does not deduplicate a matcher of one declaration against an identical matcher of an earlier declaration, and a hoist next to a twin keeps its auxiliary constants (kb/0066's count stands).

Library, not paper: lean-causal/campaign/T-abs-past-inextensible-meets-cauchy/Probe.lean imports CausalScaffold.PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy. That module's source was graduated and no longer exists, but a stale olean of it remains in .lake/build. Its import now fails with 'environment already contains Causal.Causality.PastInextensible.of_retraction.match_1_1 from Causal.CExtConnexeCauchy.SubArc'. The stale olean declares the matcher again on top of the strict SubArc it imports. The error is reported for the matcher, a def. kb/0082's silent merge of equal theorems does not cover it. The library is not affected: the gate builds the scaffold from its sources, and the stale olean has none. The probe's content (#check and #print axioms of the moved names) runs clean when retargeted at Causal.PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy, and this target's Probe.lean covers it.
kb_proposals: Update kb/0315 and kb/0244: the one-sided end-piece lemmas (PastExtensible.of_top_tail, FutureExtensible.of_top_tail, PastExtensible.of_bottom_tail), PastInextensible.of_retraction and pastExtensible_of_subArc are in Causal.CExtConnexeCauchy.SubArc (T-abs-end-pieces-one-sided; same full names). Extensible.of_top_tail is their corollary through extensible_iff, and FutureExtensible.of_top_tail is the library's one pause construction (pauseTop, exists_compress).

A hoist next to a twin with an identical term-mode matcher keeps its own matcher: Lean 4.31 does not share `<decl>.match_1_1` between declarations of one module, so the parent's value hash is unchanged (T-abs-end-pieces-one-sided: PastInextensible.of_retraction next to Inextensible.of_retraction).

After a hoist out of a graduated module, an old campaign probe that imports the graduated module's scaffold name (`import CausalScaffold.X`) may fail on a stale .lake olean. A matcher (a def) declared twice is an import error, unlike two equal theorems (kb/0082). Retarget the probe at the strict module; do not rebuild the scaffold name.
